newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Japanese firms said rethinking Israel investment.
newsitem.headline: Japanese firms said rethinking Israel investment.

text.p: Japanese business is taking a wait-and-see attitude about investing in Israel because of the slowdown in the peace process, said Shmuel Harlap, chairman of Calmobil Group, the Israeli importer and distributor for Mitsubishi Motors.
"The slowdown of the (Middle East) peace process has led many Japanese companies to rethink their policy," Harlap said, adding that he had had similar indications from Mitsubishi.
Direct Japanese investment in Israel last year reached $25 million, mostly in Israel's high-tech sector.
Harlap said a number of investments by Japanese companies had been put on hold in recent months.
Calmobil is the largest importer of cars to Israel.
Until the early 1990s Japanese car makers except for Subaru did not sell to Israel because of an Arab League boycott on doing business with the Jewish state.
Advances in the peace process led to a partial lifting of the boycott.
